memory interference is a distinct and important component of memory processing that can have both negative and positive consequences for the retention of memories.

memory interference is a robust and pervasive aspect of memory processing and that off-line processing during both consolidation and reconsolidation is an important mechanism by which interference can be modulated.

the brain's memory system is more complex than was previously believed, and that this complexity is an important factor in the way that we learn and remember.

interference is not a nuisance, but rather a critical component of memory processing.
